name: Belfry of Bruges
scaleNote: 1 stud per metre. 83 m over a market hall 84 m deep: the tower and the hall are the same size and that is the point of the silhouette.

height.source: Wikipedia, Belfry of Bruges: '83 metres (272 ft)' -- the height after the wooden spire was lost to fire in 1741.

hallWidth.source: Wikipedia, Belfry of Bruges: the adjoining rectangular building is '44 metres (144 ft) broad but 84 metres (276 ft) deep'.

hallDepth.source: Wikipedia, Belfry of Bruges: '44 metres (144 ft) broad but 84 metres (276 ft) deep'.

lean.source: Wikipedia, Belfry of Bruges: the tower 'leans 87 centimetres (34 in) to the east'.

note:
THE LEAN IS CITED AND NOT BUILT. 87 cm over 83 m is 0.6 degrees, and at 1 stud/m that is under one stud of displacement at the top -- below the grid this whole project is built on. It is in `dimensions` because it is a real measured property of the building, and it is absent from the model because a stud grid cannot express it. That pair is the honest way to carry a figure you cannot build.

366 STEPS, NOT BUILT: 83 m over 366 steps is 0.23 m each, under a plate -- the same arithmetic that left Chichen Itza's 365 unbuilt.

The tower lost 19 m in 1741: it was '102 metres (335 ft)' with its wooden spire and is 83 m without. The Atlas builds the surviving 83.

Der Turm stand im ersten Entwurf vier Meter tief in der Tuchhalle -- 288 Ueberlappungen. Turm und Halle beruehren sich in Bruegge, sie durchdringen sich nicht.
